subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox container exits immediately when no-new-privileges is applied (exec /usr/bin/sleep: operation not permitted)

question: Should OpenClaw support an explicit Docker sandbox recovery path for hosts where `--security-opt no-new-privileges` prevents the sandbox container from executing `/usr/bin/sleep`?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible and user-impacting, but the practical recovery path may weaken Docker sandbox hardening, so automation should not choose the policy boundary alone.

options.title: Add explicit dangerous opt-out
options.body: Keep the secure default and add a clearly named `sandbox.docker` opt-out with dangerous-config reporting, docs, tests, and real Docker proof for the incompatible-host case.

options.title: Improve diagnostics only
options.body: Keep hardening unconditional and add status/session/doctor guidance so affected hosts get a precise error and supported mitigation without weakening the sandbox.

options.title: Declare affected hosts unsupported
options.body: Treat hosts that reject Docker `no-new-privileges` as unsupported for Docker sandbox mode and direct users to another backend or host configuration.

recommendation.title: Add explicit dangerous opt-out
recommendation.body: Keep the secure default and add a clearly named `sandbox.docker` opt-out with dangerous-config reporting, docs, tests, and real Docker proof for the incompatible-host case.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice extends the dangerous Docker override and sandbox security-boundary pattern that steipete recently shaped.
